subject: Follow-up: Embeddings fit validation & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Rivers <trivers@acme.com>, Priya Desai <pdesai@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: embeddings fit & proposed next steps

Hi Tom / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can validate model fit for Acme's search use case:

What we heard
- Primary goal: improve semantic search relevance across product docs + support tickets (long tail of paraphrases).
- Current baseline: Elasticsearch BM25 + small dense vectors from vendor A (384d). You saw ~60-65% relevance on manual QA set.
- Constraints: 100k document corpus, 128k monthly queries, 75ms median inference latency target for query-side embedding generation, and storage/cost sensitivity for embedding dimensionality.

Recommended evaluation plan
1) Models to test: redwood-embed-512 (512-d FP16), redwood-embed-256 (256-d int8 quantized), and a compact baseline: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-d).
2) Metrics we'll compute: Precision@10, Recall@50, MRR, average cosine similarity (positives), and latency/throughput for batched queries. We'll also run drift snapshots vs your historical query set.
3) Acceptance criteria (proposal): Precision@10 >= 0.75 OR MRR >= 0.6, and query-side median latency <= 80ms for batched requests at QPS=10.
4) Prompt / query set: you shared a small sample on the call — please confirm the attached acme-sample-queries.csv is representative. We'll run full eval once we get the 1k labeled pairs (or we can seed with our synthetic augmentation if labeling takes longer).

Attachments included: acme-embeddings-benchmarks.csv (example output from our sandbox), prompt-sets-v1.json (initial prompt/normalization rules), acme-sample-queries.csv

Next steps
- Tom/Priya: confirm sample represents your traffic and share any additional labeled positives/negatives (1–2 days).
- We (Redwood): run a 3-model comparison and share a short eval report with top-K examples and metric table (3 business days after we have labeled pairs / approval to augment).
- Optional: if you want a lightweight A/B on your staging index, we can demo retrieval results and integrate with your QA tooling.

Notes on dimensionality / drift:
- 512-d embeddings tend to give better separation on paraphrase-heavy corpora; cost/storage is roughly ~33% higher vs 384-d at full precision, but quantized 256-d int8 can be competitive for recall-focused tasks.
- We'll include a drift monitor: simple distributional shift (cosine mean/std) plus sample-based embedding clustering to detect semantic drift over time.

I'll schedule a 30-min checkpoint after we deliver the eval report. Thanks again — excited to help validate fit.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0192
https://redwood.ai

---

(On the call we also flagged privacy: if any queries/documents are sensitive, let us know — we can run evaluation in a private VPC instance.)

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A couple quick clarifying questions before we hand this to our ML ops team:

1) Dimensionality tradeoff: can you give a rough expected storage and latency delta between redwood-embed-512 (FP16) vs 256 int8? Our index is stored in-house and we need to budget storage.
2) For the acceptance criteria: how strict should we be on Precision@10 vs MRR? We are particularly sensitive to false positives surfacing in support searches.
3) Can you run the eval on our small sample (attached) and provide the top-5 retrievals per query so we can eyeball qualitative results?

Attaching a 200-row sample (acme-sample-queries.csv) that reflects recent support queries. If possible, we'd like the initial eval results in <5 business days.

Thanks — Tom

Hi all — copying in engineering for the eval run plan. Suggested concrete approach from our side:

Proposed eval details (we can adjust):
- Models to run: redwood-embed-512-fp16 (512-d), redwood-embed-256-int8 (256-d quant), sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-d baseline).
- Dataset: use Tom's 200-row sample as quick sanity + we will run with label-augmentation to reach ~1k pairs if Acme can't provide labeled positives/negatives right away.
- Metrics: Precision@10, Recall@50, MRR, nDCG@10, False Positive Rate (for support), average cosine similarity for labeled positives, and latency at QPS=5/10 for batched inference (batch size 16/32).
- Acceptance thresholds (initial): Precision@10 >= 0.72, Recall@50 >= 0.88, MRR >= 0.58, FP rate <= 0.15 for top-10. These are tunable once we see the data.
- Drift check: compute mean/std of cosine distances vs historical queries and a silhouette score on 10-cluster embedding KMeans to detect representation drift. If silhouette drops >0.1 vs baseline, flag for review.

Operational notes:
- Storage: rough estimate — 512-d FP16 ~= 1KB per vector; 256-d int8 ~= 256 bytes/vector. For 100k docs: 512-d FP16 ~100MB, 256-d int8 ~25MB (these are index storages ignoring overhead/IVF structures). We'll provide a more precise footprint after the eval.
- Latency: for query-side embedding gen: expected median latency for 512-d FP16 on our hosted instance (g4dn-like) at batch=16 is ~40-60ms; 256-int8 often reduces compute latency by ~20-30%. We will measure on your QPS profile.
- Quality regression: we'll run a small baseline regression check comparing vendor A vectors and our models to ensure no drop in key intents. If we detect regressions (delta MRR < -0.05), we'll surface PRs and recommended prompt/normalization changes.

Timeline: once we have the 200-row sample and confirmation to augment, engineering can deliver a short eval report with metrics + top-K examples in 3 business days. If Acme wants a staged A/B, that is a separate 1-week integration effort.

Marissa — can you confirm whether Acme prefers augmentation or will label to 1k? Also, Tom/Priya: is running this in a Redwood-hosted sandbox okay or do you require private VPC?

Thanks,
Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
